neighbours.label: the slot right before a delighted verdict on how something just tasted or felt in the body ('the flavor was', 'the feeling was', or 'mmm' / 'oh my' after a bite), setting up words like 'perfect' or 'heavenly'; quiet when the verdict is on a non-sensory thing (the bill, the service, a person, a TV episode) or the setup promises a bad taste
neighbours.short: slot before a delighted taste/feel verdict
fire: I took one bite of the chocolate tart and the flavor was absolutely heavenly.
Mmm, oh my, this mango is perfect.
After the long hike, the feeling of that hot shower on my back was pure bliss.
She sipped the fresh espresso and sighed, 'Oh my, that is divine.'
The broth was rich and the taste was simply perfect.
Sinking into the warm bath, the sensation was heavenly.
He bit into the warm croissant and murmured, 'Mmm, that's incredible.'
The first spoonful of the ripe peach sorbet tasted like heaven.
quiet: "We have been preparing for years for a successful landing by Curiosity, and all signs are good," Dave Lavery, MSL programme executive, said.
We ordered the lamb with mint sauce and the waiter was a student.
I took one look at the restaurant bill and the total was absolutely outrageous.
Mmm, I think the waiter forgot our order again.
After the long hike, the view from the ridge was something we photographed.
She read the final episode recap and sighed, 'That ending was so rushed.'
The broth had gone cold and the taste was sour and metallic.
Sinking into the old chair, I realized the meeting would run late.

predictions: blind test written label-only by a second author; cold mission (labelled from own tops and probes, no feeder lookup). Risk: sentence-initial 'Mmm' in a near miss.
